A.explanation: Radio waves have the longest wavelengths in the spectrum, typically greater than $0.1 \text{ m}$, which is about $10^9$ times larger than $138 \text{ pm}$.

B.explanation: Microwaves have wavelengths of order millimetres to centimetres, around $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-1} \text{ m}$, far larger than $138 \text{ pm}$.

C.explanation: Visible light has wavelengths around $400-700 \text{ nm}$, which is about $1000$ times larger than $138 \text{ pm}$.

D.explanation: $138 \text{ pm} = 1.38 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$, which lies in the $10^{-11} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$ range characteristic of X-rays.

hints: Convert the given $138 \text{ pm}$ into metres using $1 \text{ pm} = 10^{-12} \text{ m}$ and notice how small the result is.
Recall the order of the electromagnetic spectrum by wavelength, from long radio waves and microwaves down through visible light to very short X-rays and gamma rays.
Compare your value near $10^{-10} \text{ m}$ with the familiar scale of visible light at about $10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to decide which region it fits.
walkthrough: Note the given wavelength is $138 \text{ pm}$ in a vacuum, so convert to SI units: $\lambda = 138 \times 10^{-12} \text{ m} = 1.38 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$.

Recall the approximate wavelength ranges: radio waves $> 0.1 \text{ m}$, microwaves $10^{-3} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-1} \text{ m}$, visible light $4 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ to $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$, X-rays about $10^{-11} \text{ m}$ to $10^{-8} \text{ m}$.
Compare $1.38 \times 10^{-10} \text{ m}$ with these ranges: it is much smaller than visible light by a factor of about $1000$ and much smaller than microwaves and radio waves.
It falls squarely in the X-ray band of very short wavelength and high frequency electromagnetic radiation.
